pr_title: Improve handling of unrecoverable storage corruption
pr_body: ## Proposed change If core storage gets corrupted, currently core will boot loop in many cases. If its an integration specific file, the integration will usually fail to start or break in an undefined manner. We now complain loudly in the log, move away the corrupt data and start fresh to allow startup to proceed so the user can get to the UI and restore from backup without having to attach a console (or otherwise login to the OS and manually modify files). Anything that is not a `JSONDecodeError` such as `OSError` is still treated as fatal as thats usually indicative of a hardware or system problem and not an unclean shutdown. That still seems preferable since the most likely outcome of a boot loop is the user spending hours trying to figure out how to recover the system which would likely be significantly more painful. We also create a notification to ensure the user does not miss this as its quite critical that they address the problem as it may be an indication of something larger. fixes #96574 ## Type of change - [ ] Dependency upgrade - [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New integration (thank you!) - [ ] New feature (which adds functionality to an existing integration) - [ ] Deprecation (breaking change to happen in the future) - [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break) - [x] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests ## Additional information - This PR fixes or closes issue: fixes # - This PR is related to issue: - Link to documentation pull request: ## Checklist - [x] The code change is tested and works locally. - [ ] Local tests pass. **Your PR cannot be merged unless tests pass** - [ ] There is no commented out code in this PR. - [ ] I have followed the [development checklist][dev-checklist] - [ ] I have followed the [perfect PR recommendations][perfect-pr] - [ ] The code has been formatted using Black (`black --fast homeassistant tests`) - [x] Tests have been added to verify that the new code works. Updated and included derived files by running: `python3 -m script.hassfest`. - [ ] New or updated dependencies have been added to `requirements_all.txt`. review_comments:
We prefer if the user can "fix" persistent issues instead of just ignoring.
It means `is_fixable` should be True and the issue translations should have a `fix_flow`.
Note: There's no need to implement an actual flow handler, the default flow handler will just show the `fix_flow`.

For example https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/4a6247f922a41f3145a30b1e071aa92f1dcdd1f1/homeassistant/components/automation/strings.json#L38-L46

We may want to set the issue_domain according to the storage key, something like:
```py
issue_domain = HOMEASSISTANT_DOMAIN
if len(store_domain := self.key.split(".",1)) > 1 and store_domain[0] != "core:
    issue_domain = store_domain[0]
```

But maybe this is not reliable, I'm not sure if we enforce this pattern consistently.
I think we could validate the domain exists in hass.config.components and use it if it does, otherwise fallback to the home assistant domain.  Will see how that works
